claims.text: Eutectic high-entropy alloys feature dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries.
Internal lamellar-colony boundaries act as microcrack nucleation sites during room-temperature tensile deformation.
Optimized laser shock peening induces localized compressive residual stresses at internal lamellar-colony boundaries.
Optimized laser shock peening refines the microstructure of internal lamellar-colony boundaries.
Peening produces improved nanostructural cohesion at internal lamellar-colony boundaries.
Compressive residual stresses and boundary refinement reduce stress concentrations.
Reduced stress concentrations delay or prevent microcrack nucleation under tensile loading.
Laser shock peening suppresses microcrack propagation under tensile loading.
Laser-shock-peened specimens will have higher tensile strength than untreated specimens.
Laser-shock-peened specimens will have greater room-temperature tensile ductility than untreated specimens.
Laser-shock-peened specimens will exhibit delayed microcrack onset relative to untreated specimens.
Laser-shock-peened specimens will exhibit a lower microcrack density than untreated specimens.
Peening intensities that are excessively high or low may fail to produce the desired interfacial modifications.
Processing deviations or unsuitable peening intensities may be detrimental to mechanical properties.
